source: No published manifest matches current origin/main (e9e6b3c). Release v0.1.0-fc52718 has no package list; the only one is PACKAGES.txt in release sources-v0.1.0-618726b (older commit, ~828 packages). So I replayed build/forge's apt operations in ubuntu:24.04 on homebase: sources noble, noble-updates and noble-security as forge writes them; base = debootstrap minbase (91 packages, matches debootstrap --print-debs); pin_no_snap; full-upgrade; one 'apt-get install --no-install-recommends' of locales + packages_hardware/boot/base/security/desktop/files (from origin/main profiles/desktop.profile, which now includes librsvg2-common) + fonts-noto-cjk (fonts_cjk=yes); packages_exclude purge; Firefox from packages.mozilla.org (158.0.1~build1, no Recommends); gnome-software+packagekit+appstream; flatpak+gnome-software-plugin-flatpak+xdg-desktop-portal(+gtk); stage 3 build deps, purge and autoremove (libwayland-server0 and libxkbcommon0 kept); stage 4 aurosicons stub, purge of ubuntu-mono and humanity-icon-theme; harden's cups-browsed purge. Final state: 879 packages, dpkg audit clean. The count includes the aurosicons stub; it excludes the 7 AurOS-built packages (auros, auros-archive-keyring, -bootchain, -config, -desktop, -ferry, -first) that stage 6 adds. Their only Recommends are python3-cryptography and efibootmgr, both installed. Cross-check against PACKAGES.txt (618726b): identical except for changes since then (new: chrony, exfatprogs, ipp-usb, libnss-mdns, fonts-atkinson-hyperlegible, librsvg2-common, the LibreOffice Writer/Calc stack with carlito/caladea, heif-gdk-pixbuf, libheif-plugin-libde265, aurosicons; gone: fonts-inter, ubuntu-mono, humanity-icon-theme, and the binutils family of 7 that the old image kept). 'dropped' lists the 87 distinct unsatisfied Recommends groups (direct Recommends of installed packages only, as asked). A group counts as satisfied if any alternative is installed or provided by an installed package; version constraints were ignored. I name the package apt would install first. Entries tagged DELIBERATE, HANDLED, KNOWN or UNRESOLVABLE need no action. DELIBERATE PURGES AND PINS in build/forge, for the judges: (1) packages_exclude 'snapd ubuntu-advantage-tools popularity-contest' is a no-op, since none is installed without recommends. ubuntu-pro-client stays because gnome-software needs software-properties-gtk, which needs it; rootfs 20apt-esm-hook.conf neutralises its hook. (2) pin_no_snap pins snapd, and Ubuntu's firefox*, thunderbird*, chromium-browser*, chromium-chromedriver* and chromium-codecs-ffmpeg*, to -1; purge_snap_leftovers is a no-op here. (3) packages.mozilla.org supplies firefox* only (pin 1000; -1 for everything else). (4) trim_server_firmware removes mellanox-spectrum, marvell-prestera, netronome and qlogic if present; they are not installed. (5) Stage 3 installs gcc, libc6-dev, make, pkg-config, libdbus-1-dev, libwayland-dev, libwayland-bin, wayland-protocols and libxkbcommon-dev, then purges them and autoremoves 44 packages; none was a Recommends target. (6) unbrand_icons swaps ubuntu-mono and humanity-icon-theme for the empty stub aurosicons (Provides ubuntu-mono) and pins both to -1. (7) build/harden purges cups-browsed if present; it was never installed. (8) The profile comment drops mesa-vulkan-drivers on purpose. (9) rootfs 10-dns-resolved.conf (dns=default) covers the absence of systemd-resolved. (10) rootfs apt preferences 'auros' let AurOS's repository supply auros* only. Caveats: the docker base differs from minbase only by unminimize and usrmerge. Versions are noble-updates as of 2026-10-24. My notes on what each package does come from apt metadata, `dpkg -c` listings and repo greps; they are not tests.

findings.what_breaks: The image has no thumbnail service at all. Thunar (her Files) and Ristretto (her Photos) both request thumbnails over the D-Bus name org.freedesktop.thumbnails.Thumbnailer1, and nothing installed provides it, so every picture, iPhone HEIC photo and PDF in a folder is drawn as a generic icon. Ristretto's thumbnail strip is the same.
findings.how_she_notices: She opens Pictures or Downloads in Files and sees rows of identical grey 'image' and 'document' icons, so she cannot tell which photo is the grandchild's without opening each one. Open/Attach/Upload dialogs in Firefox and LibreOffice also show no previews. GTK file choosers only display thumbnails that already exist in ~/.cache/thumbnails, and nothing creates them.
findings.evidence: Measured by installing the resolved desktop profile in a noble container (profile + forge lists + gnome-software/flatpak/portal-gtk, --no-install-recommends, 833 packages). Not installed: tumbler, tumbler-common, libtumbler-1-0t64. grep -a on /usr/bin/thunar and /usr/bin/ristretto shows both use org.freedesktop.thumbnails.Thumbnailer1. /usr/share/dbus-1/services has no thumbnails service. gdbus call to that name returns 'ServiceUnknown: not provided by any .service files'. The only *.thumbnailer files on the image are evince.thumbnailer and librsvg.thumbnailer, and tumbler 4.18.1 has no xdg-thumbnailer plugin, so nothing reads them. After installing just `tumbler`, tumblerd D-Bus-activates and GetSupported lists image/jpeg, png, heic, heif, avif, application/pdf and fonts. Queueing a PNG and a PDF produced thumbnails in ~/.cache/thumbnails/normal. HEIC support comes from the already-installed heif-gdk-pixbuf, and its deps (libpoppler-glib8t64, libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-0, libjpeg8, libfreetype6, libxfce4util7) are all in the image already. In the repo, grep -i tumbler over build/ profiles/ rootfs/ src/ tools/ finds nothing. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md WP-25 lists tumbler as to be added, and docs/results/sites.md row 25 says '(WP-25 adds the thumbnailer)'. The profile and tools/everydaytest.sh took the other WP-25 packages (carlito, caladea, heif-gdk-pixbuf, libreoffice-*) but not tumbler. Also checked and cleared, no action: libgdk-pixbuf2.0-bin (only gdk-pixbuf-csource/pixdata/thumbnailer plus a .thumbnailer file no installed service reads; query-loaders is in libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 and loaders.cache lists svg and heif), libgtk-3-bin and libgtk-4-bin (gtk-launch, gtk-query-settings, gtk4-update-icon-cache and similar; no installed package or repo file calls them, and gtk-update-icon-cache IS installed), colord (no cupsd/ristretto/evince/LibreOffice link; cupsd talks to it over D-Bus only if present), libheif-plugin-aomenc (encode only; aomdec and libde265 are installed and loaders.cache's heif entry covers heic/heif/avif), mesa-vulkan-drivers (deliberate; Xwayland etc. do not need it), xfonts-base (Xwayland is started -rootless, and libXfont2 has built-in 'fixed' and 'cursor'), fonts-droid-fallback (only Ghostscript's last-resort CID substitute), default-libdecor-0-plugin-1 (Xwayland runs -rootless and aurwl implements xdg-decoration), gstreamer1.0-gtk3 (only for LibreOffice's avmedia-gstreamer backend, which is not installed), cursor theme (Adwaita cursors present, default theme alternative resolves).
findings.fix: Add `tumbler` to packages_files in profiles/desktop.profile (inherited by the office and revive profiles), with a comment saying why. Add it to the package list in tools/everydaytest.sh so a regression is caught. Do NOT add tumbler-plugins-extra: it Depends libgepub, which pulls libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 and libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-0 (the ~144 MB WebKit the profile already removed when it swapped atril for evince), about 25 more packages in all. Video thumbnails are the only thing given up.
findings.cost_mb: about 1.1 MB installed (tumbler 0.37 + tumbler-common 0.59 + libtumbler-1-0t64 0.10), 0.16 MB download, 3 packages and no new dependencies. tumblerd used about 30 MB RSS after thumbnailing a PNG and a PDF.

findings.recommended_by: ristretto (Suggests, not a Recommends; an adjacent gap found while checking the pixbuf loaders)
findings.what_breaks: gdk-pixbuf has no WebP loader. loaders.cache lists ani, bmp, gif, heif, icns, ico, pnm, qtif, svg, tga, tiff, xbm, xpm, plus built-in png and jpeg. build/forge's stage_file_types nevertheless sets image/webp=org.xfce.ristretto.desktop, and Ristretto decodes through gdk-pixbuf, so a .webp she double-clicks opens in Photos but cannot be decoded. Thunar/tumbler also cannot thumbnail it.
findings.how_she_notices: A picture saved from a web page (Google Images, Facebook, Pinterest and similar often save as .webp) will not open in Photos. She gets an error or a blank window where a picture should be.
findings.evidence: In the simulated image (see tumbler finding), webp-pixbuf-loader is absent and libgdk_pixbuf loaders.cache has no pixbufloader-webp. ldd /usr/bin/ristretto shows it links libgdk_pixbuf-2.0 and libexif. apt-cache depends ristretto shows 'Suggests: webp-pixbuf-loader' (and heif/avif/jxl loaders; heif is already added by the profile for the same reason). build/forge lines ~577-584 map image/webp and image/heic to Ristretto. With tumbler installed, GetSupported lacked image/webp and a .webp (made with cwebp) got no thumbnail. After `apt-get install --no-install-recommends webp-pixbuf-loader`, the postinst trigger put pixbufloader-webp into loaders.cache, GetSupported listed image/webp, and the .webp thumbnail was created. No existing hardentest check covers this, because hardentest.sh only asserts the SVG loader. Firefox and LibreOffice decode WebP themselves, so only Photos and Files are affected.
findings.fix: Add webp-pixbuf-loader to packages_files in profiles/desktop.profile next to heif-gdk-pixbuf, with a one-line comment. Optionally extend tools/hardentest.sh's loader check to also require the webp (and heif) entry in loaders.cache.
findings.cost_mb: about 0.09 MB installed (webp-pixbuf-loader 43 KB + libwebpdemux2 44 KB; libwebp7 and libwebpmux3 are already installed), 24 KB download.

findings.what_breaks: No VA-API driver is installed. mpv is unaffected, since its default is hwdec=no and no repo file sets it. Firefox is affected: it uses VA-API hardware decoding by default on Intel GPUs since Firefox 115 and on AMD since Firefox 136, and the pinned firefox_version is 140. Without a driver it falls back silently to CPU decoding. That is the 'choppy video on an old laptop' case, but only on machines where the GPU would have decoded the codec in hardware. I could not run Firefox on a GPU, so the size of the effect is unmeasured.
findings.how_she_notices: Web video such as news clips or YouTube on a 2013-era dual-core laptop drops frames and runs the fan, while the same machine would play it smoothly with hardware decode.
findings.evidence: Simulated image: libva2, libva-drm2, libva-x11-2, libva-wayland2 and libavcodec60 (via mpv) are installed, but va-driver-all, mesa-va-drivers, i965-va-driver and intel-media-va-driver are all absent. `mpv --no-config --list-options` shows '--hwdec String list (default: no)'. grep for hwdec, vaapi and mpv.conf over build, rootfs, profiles, src and tools finds nothing. The Firefox defaults come from Phoronix/OMG!Ubuntu coverage of Firefox 115 and 136, not from Mozilla's release notes. apt -s install va-driver-all adds intel-media-va-driver (13.3 MB), libigdgmm12, i965-va-driver (1.8 MB) and mesa-va-drivers (0.05 MB). vdpau-driver-all (mesa-vdpau-drivers) only serves legacy VDPAU clients, which neither mpv nor Firefox use here, so skip it.
findings.fix: Optional, and worth deciding with the media judge. Add i965-va-driver and mesa-va-drivers (about 1.9 MB) to packages_desktop: this covers Intel up to about Kaby Lake plus AMD, which is the target hardware. Add intel-media-va-driver (13 MB) only if 2016+ Intel laptops matter. Update the profile's comment about hardware decode accordingly.
findings.cost_mb: 1.9 MB for i965-va-driver + mesa-va-drivers; about 15 MB for full va-driver-all (intel-media-va-driver 13.3 MB + libigdgmm12 + i965 1.8 MB + mesa 0.05 MB)

findings.what_breaks: GNOME Software 46 (the only GTK4 program in the image) plays an app's AppStream screenshot videos through GtkVideo. GTK4 loads the GStreamer media backend from /usr/lib/.../gtk-4.0/4.0.0/media/, and that directory does not exist on the image, so those video screenshots cannot play. Adding only this package would not fix it, because gstreamer1.0-plugins-good (webm/mp4 demux, VP8/VP9) is also absent. Few apps ship a screenshot video, so this affects only some store pages.
findings.how_she_notices: On a store page for an app that has a demo video, the screenshot area stays blank or shows an error instead of playing.
findings.evidence: /usr/bin/gnome-software contains the strings 'Failed to download screenshot video', as_screenshot_get_videos, GtkVideo and gtk_video_set_filename. Only gnome-software and libadwaita are GTK4 users in the image. find /usr/lib -path '*gtk-4.0*' -name '*.so' finds only the cups and file print backends. gstreamer1.0-plugins-good is absent, and the sim shows adding it plus the module brings about 15 packages. libgtk-4-bin is not needed (gtk4-launch, gtk4-update-icon-cache etc. have no callers), and the GTK3 sibling gstreamer1.0-gtk3 is moot because libreoffice-avmedia-backend-gstreamer is not installed.
findings.fix: Leave as is unless store video previews matter. To enable them, add libgtk-4-media-gstreamer and gstreamer1.0-plugins-good (plus gstreamer1.0-libav if H.264 previews are wanted). Otherwise record it as a deliberate omission in the profile comments.
findings.cost_mb: 0.25 MB for libgtk-4-media-gstreamer alone, which is insufficient; about 11-12 MB installed with gstreamer1.0-plugins-good and its new dependencies (libgstreamer-gl1.0-0, libtag1v5, libv4l, libwavpack1, libshout3, libgpm2, libncurses6 and others); plus 0.28 MB for gstreamer1.0-libav.

findings.what_breaks: Word documents set in Arial Narrow are not reflowed horizontally, but they do get taller lines. fontconfig and LibreOffice already substitute Nimbus Sans Narrow (from fonts-urw-base35, which libgs10-common Depends on), which has the same advance widths. Its line height is about 12% larger than Liberation Sans Narrow's. A form or table built in Arial Narrow can grow a few lines and push content onto the next page.
findings.how_she_notices: Rarely: a downloaded or emailed Word form or table that used Arial Narrow comes out slightly longer, or its last row spills to a new page.
findings.evidence: Simulated image: fc-match 'Arial Narrow' gives Nimbus Sans Narrow:Regular, and fonts-liberation-sans-narrow is absent. I converted a test flat ODT (Arial Narrow 12 pt line, 3 words wide ~230 pt) to PDF with LibreOffice 24.2 headless. Before: pdffonts shows NimbusSansNarrow-Regular, and the last word 'dog' on line 1 ends at x=287.908, with a line pitch of 14.4 pt. After installing fonts-liberation-sans-narrow: LiberationSansNarrow, 'dog' ends at x=288.436 (0.5 pt apart over a 230 pt line, so line breaks are identical), and the line pitch is 12.85 pt. Calibri and Cambria map to Carlito and Caladea, and Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New map to Liberation, so only Arial Narrow is affected. Verdana, Tahoma and Georgia fall to DejaVu in every case, since no metric clone exists in the archive.
findings.fix: Optional: add fonts-liberation-sans-narrow to packages_base next to the other fonts-* entries if exact Word pagination matters. The horizontal damage is already covered, so skipping it is defensible.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. I simulated apt --no-install-recommends on the full desktop profile plus store and flatpak (776 packages to install, about 865 with the base). tumbler, tumbler-common and libtumbler-1-0t64 are absent, and no package in that set Depends on them. The only relations are Recommends from thunar 4.18.8 and ristretto 0.13.1. Neither program can thumbnail without it. I read their sources: thunar/thunar-thumbnailer.c and ristretto/src/thumbnailer.c call only org.freedesktop.thumbnails.Thumbnailer1 through tumbler, and Thunar has no in-process fallback for local files. In a real install of thunar, ristretto, evince, gvfs and gnome-software, no D-Bus service file provides that name. The only *.thumbnailer files are evince's and librsvg's, and nothing reads them. In the repo, grep -i tumbler over build, profiles, rootfs, src and tools on origin/main finds nothing. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md still lists tumbler as a package to add, and the older docs/results/build-all.txt lists it under Recommended packages not installed. forge installs with --no-install-recommends everywhere, and thunar is her "Your files" and ristretto her "Photos", so she would see grey generic icons for every picture and PDF. The fix is cheap: 3 packages, about 1 MB. Do not add tumbler-plugins-extra (the finding says it pulls WebKit; I did not re-verify that).

Confirmed. In a real install of ristretto, heif-gdk-pixbuf, librsvg2-common and gnome-software with no recommends, GdkPixbuf.Pixbuf.get_formats() returns only ani, bmp, gif, heif/avif, icns, ico, jpeg, png, pnm, qtif, svg, tga, tiff, xbm and xpm. A real .webp made with cwebp fails to load with "Couldn't recognize the image file format", while the same image as PNG loads fine. ristretto 0.13.1 does not link libwebp (ldd and strings both clean), so it decodes only through gdk-pixbuf. apt-cache shows ristretto only Suggests webp-pixbuf-loader, and nothing else in the closure provides a WebP loader. build/forge maps image/webp to org.xfce.ristretto.desktop, so a double-clicked .webp goes to the one program that cannot read it. It is reachable because web pages often save images as WebP. The effect is real but moderate, not high. Cost is about 0.1 MB. Firefox and LibreOffice decode WebP themselves, so only Photos and Files are affected.

Unconfirmed, and the repo gives good reason to think it has no effect. The drivers are indeed absent (libva2 only Recommends va-driver-all, and none is in the closure), and mpv defaults to hwdec=no. But the finding admits it never ran Firefox on a GPU, so the effect is unmeasured. src/aurwl/aurwl.c states the compositor accepts wl_shm buffers only, with no dmabuf and no GL at all (it posts a protocol error for any non-shm buffer). Firefox's VA-API path hands decoded frames to the compositor as DMABuf surfaces and, per web sources I found (anecdotal, not Mozilla docs), needs hardware WebRender. On a CPU-only compositor with llvmpipe, Firefox should fall back to software decode whether or not a VA driver is installed. A VA driver would add 2 to 15 MB and change nothing she could see. Not worth acting on without a real-hardware test.

The mechanism is real but she would almost never hit it, so I am calling it unconfirmed as a user-facing break. libgtk-4-1 Recommends libgtk-4-media-gstreamer and it is absent. gnome-software 46.0 src/gs-screenshot-image.c does call gtk_video_set_filename, but only when a screenshot's media kind is AS_SCREENSHOT_MEDIA_KIND_VIDEO. Ordinary image screenshots and every symbolic icon are unaffected. I found no evidence that Flathub or Ubuntu AppStream data commonly carries screenshot videos, and I could not measure how many do. The fix is also incomplete and costs about 12 MB, because gstreamer1.0-plugins-good is needed as well. Record it as a deliberate omission rather than fixing it.

Something else provides the font, and the rest is a rare, cosmetic effect. In a real install of the profile's font set, fc-match "Arial Narrow" returns Nimbus Sans Narrow (NimbusSansNarrow-Regular.pfb). fonts-urw-base35 is in the simulated closure through libgs10-common, so widths and line breaks are preserved, as the finding itself says. What is left is a slightly taller line pitch in Word documents that use Arial Narrow, which very few of her documents would. I did not re-measure the 12% line-height difference. Calibri, Cambria, Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New already map to metric-compatible fonts. Adding 0.5 MB is harmless but unneeded.

findings.recommended_by: pipewire-pulse and wireplumber (Suggests only, so it is not on the dropped-Recommends list; found by tracing the Bluetooth-headphones path)
findings.what_breaks: Bluetooth headphones and speakers pair and show Connected, but PipeWire has no Bluetooth audio plugin, so no sound device ever appears. Sound keeps coming out of the laptop speakers. bluez is installed and the shell has a Headphones and mice panel, so the feature looks present but is dead.
findings.how_she_notices: She pairs her wireless headphones in Settings, the panel says Connected, she plays a song and it still plays from the laptop speakers, or she hears nothing.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in a noble container holding the desktop+files+store package set installed with --no-install-recommends (842 packages). WirePlumber 0.4.17 with the bluez monitor's logind gating disabled logs: "SPA handle 'api.bluez5.enum.dbus' could not be loaded; is it installed?" followed by "PipeWire's BlueZ SPA missing or broken. Bluetooth not supported." After installing libspa-0.2-bluetooth the same run loads the plugin and its codec loaders (sbc, lc3, ldac). The container has no system bus, so it then stops at "failed to get dbus connection"; I could not test a real device. The only file providing that factory is /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/spa-0.2/bluez5/libspa-bluez5.so. src/aurshell/bt.c pairs and connects only through bluetoothctl and reads "Connected: yes", so the panel says Connected without any audio check. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md WP-25 says "add libspa-0.2-bluetooth" and the day-1 checklist says "Bluetooth headphones play sound". At origin/main b28851a, git grep for libspa|a2dp|bluez5 over build, profiles, rootfs and tools finds no libspa, and profiles/desktop.profile does not list it.
findings.fix: Add libspa-0.2-bluetooth to packages_desktop in profiles/desktop.profile, next to pipewire, pipewire-pulse and wireplumber. Add a tools/imagetest-style assertion that libspa-bluez5.so exists in the image.
findings.cost_mb: 1.4 MB installed / 0.4 MB download (6 packages: libspa-0.2-bluetooth plus libfreeaptx0, libsbc1, liblc3-1, libldacbt-enc2, libldacbt-abr2)

findings.what_breaks: PipeWire, WirePlumber and pipewire-pulse run at ordinary scheduling priority, with no realtime and no nice boost. Sound works, but the audio thread can starve and crackle or drop out when the CPU is busy. That is the normal state of the 2013-era laptops this targets: software H.264 decode in mpv or Firefox, plus a CPU-only compositor.
findings.how_she_notices: Crackling or stuttering audio while a film or video call runs and the machine is working hard. Everything is fine when the machine is idle.
findings.evidence: pipewire 1.0.5 module-rt run as an unprivileged user in the same package set. Rlimit attempt: "failed to set realtime policy: Operation not permitted". Portal attempt: "Can't find org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop". With a system bus up but no rtkit: "RTKit error: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown", "RTKit does not give us MaxRealtimePriority, using 1", "MinNiceLevel, using 0", and "Realtime scheduling disabled". The rlimit fallback (/etc/security/limits.d/25-pw-rlimits.conf from pipewire-bin) only applies to group @pipewire, and build/forge AUROS_GROUPS_WANT="audio video input netdev bluetooth lpadmin" never adds that group. xdg-desktop-portal is installed, but its realtime path also ends at rtkit. rtkit ships rtkit-daemon.service (D-Bus activated), a polkit policy with allow_active and allow_inactive set to yes, and /usr/libexec/rtkit-daemon. Not measured: I could not generate CPU load or count xruns in a container.
findings.fix: Preferred: add rtkit to packages_desktop. It is the stock Ubuntu path, and build/forge seal_identity's 00-auros.preset will capture the enabled unit. Zero-package alternative: add pipewire to AUROS_GROUPS_WANT in build/forge, because pam_limits is already in rootfs/etc/pam.d/systemd-user.

findings.what_breaks: The dropped-list description is wrong: this package is not the mtp-tools CLI. Its only program file is /usr/lib/udev/mtp-probe. libmtp-common's udev rule runs that probe to recognise any MTP phone that is not already in its hwdb. With the binary missing, an Android phone whose USB id is not in the list never gets ID_MTP_DEVICE, and gvfs-mtp-volume-monitor never offers it. Cross-area: phones.
findings.how_she_notices: She plugs in her Android phone and picks File transfer on the phone. Nothing appears in Thunar's sidebar, so she cannot get her photos.
findings.evidence: dpkg -c libmtp-runtime_1.1.21-3.1ubuntu1: only ./usr/lib/udev/mtp-probe plus docs. libmtp-common (installed via gvfs-backends) ships /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/69-libmtp.rules, where line 12 handles hwdb-known devices and line 39 is PROGRAM="/usr/lib/udev/mtp-probe /sys$env{DEVPATH} $attr{busnum} $attr{devnum}" for every other device. The rules and the 5,649-line hwdb are installed, the probe is not. gvfsd-mtp and gvfs-mtp-volume-monitor are installed. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md WP-25 lists libmtp-runtime and "Phone photos import", but profiles/desktop.profile does not. I did not test a real phone.
findings.fix: Add libmtp-runtime to packages_files.

findings.what_breaks: gvfs-backends is installed with gvfs-afc-volume-monitor and gvfsd-afc, which link libimobiledevice and libusbmuxd. libimobiledevice reaches an iPhone only through the usbmuxd daemon, which is missing, along with its udev rule 39-usbmuxd.rules that starts it. An iPhone's photos therefore never appear in Thunar. Cross-area: phones.
findings.how_she_notices: She plugs in her iPhone, taps Trust, and Thunar shows nothing. The iPhone photo story the product promises fails silently.
findings.evidence: On the container image, ldd /usr/libexec/gvfs-afc-volume-monitor shows libimobiledevice-1.0.so.6, libplist and libusbmuxd-2.0.so.6, and libimobiledevice6 is installed. The usbmuxd deb ships /usr/sbin/usbmuxd, usbmuxd.service and /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/39-usbmuxd.rules, none of which are on the image. git grep over build, profiles, rootfs and pkg finds no usbmuxd. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md WP-25 lists usbmuxd, but the profile does not. I did not test a real iPhone.
findings.fix: Add usbmuxd to packages_files. The daemon is started by udev only when an Apple device is plugged in.

findings.what_breaks: No thumbnail service, so folders of photos, PDFs and videos show generic icons instead of previews. Cross-area: files. Includes the media angle, video thumbnails.
findings.how_she_notices: Her Pictures or Downloads folder is a wall of identical file icons, and Ristretto's thumbnail strip is empty. She has to open files one by one to find the photo.
findings.evidence: strings of /usr/bin/thunar and /usr/bin/ristretto show both talk only to D-Bus org.freedesktop.thumbnails.Thumbnailer1 (/org/freedesktop/thumbnails/Thumbnailer1). Ristretto even contains the text "Install Tumbler or another thumbnailing daemon". Nothing on the image implements that interface: /usr/share/thumbnailers has evince.thumbnailer and librsvg.thumbnailer, but no daemon to run them. tumbler base plugins are desktop, font, gst, jpeg, pixbuf and poppler. verdicts.reason: Confirmed. I simulated the full image set (profile lists plus store, flatpak, portal and CJK fonts, 880 packages) in a noble container. libspa-0.2-bluetooth is not in it, and nothing in build/forge installs it later. Only wireplumber and pipewire-pulse mention it, as Suggests. dpkg -c shows libspa-bluez5.so and the codec plugins are only in this package, not in libspa-0.2-modules. There is no other Bluetooth audio route: bluez-alsa and pulseaudio-module-bluetooth are not installed. WirePlumber's bluez script has the literal message "PipeWire's BlueZ SPA missing or broken. Bluetooth not supported." She would hit it. The shell has a Headphones and mice panel (bt.c), help/video-calls.html tells her to connect wireless headphones there, the installer's hardware verdict says "Your Bluetooth will work", and the day-1 checklist lists Bluetooth headphones. Adding it brings in 6 packages (libspa-0.2-bluetooth, libfreeaptx0, liblc3-1, libldacbt-abr2, libldacbt-enc2, libsbc1). I did not test a real headset.

The mechanism is confirmed, but the audible effect is not measured, so I rate it low to medium rather than medium. rtkit is absent from the closure, and only pipewire-bin recommends it. pipewire.service and wireplumber.service set no priority. The only other route is the @pipewire group rlimit file (25-pw-rlimits.conf), and build/forge's AUROS_GROUPS_WANT never adds that group. So module-rt cannot raise priority. Adding rtkit is one package, about 0.1 MB, with a D-Bus activated daemon. No one has measured xruns or crackle on slow hardware.

Mostly refuted. The package holds only /usr/lib/udev/mtp-probe, and that is a fallback. 69-libmtp.rules acts at once on any device the hwdb already marks as MTP ("If we have a hwdb entry for this device, act immediately"). The hwdb has 1,412 entries and includes the mainstream phones I checked: Pixel 18d1:4ee1, Samsung 04e8:6860, Motorola, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Huawei, OPPO, Vivo and Sony. A phone left on Photo transfer (PTP) mode would also show through gvfs-gphoto2. The gap is real only for phones missing from the hwdb, which she is unlikely to own. It costs 6 KB if the owner wants it anyway. I did not test a real phone.

Refuted. gvfs-afc does need usbmuxd, which is missing. But an iPhone's photos have a second path that is in the image. libgphoto2's udev rule (60-libgphoto2-6t64.rules) sets ID_GPHOTO2 for any device with a PTP interface (*:060101:*), and its hwdb lists the iPhone as "PTP mode". gvfs-gphoto2-volume-monitor is in gvfs-backends, and gvfs's own source has a comment about working around bugs for devices "like the iPhone". So Thunar should list the phone as a camera with its photos, with no usbmuxd. This is from reading rules and source; I did not test a real iPhone. Adding usbmuxd would make gvfs-afc take the phone over instead, and I could not test which path works better, so only add it if a real-iPhone test shows a need.

Confirmed. tumbler (and libtumbler-1-0t64 and tumbler-common) are absent from the closure, and thunar and ristretto only Recommend them. I read Thunar 4.18.8's source: it requests thumbnails only from the tumbler D-Bus service, with no internal fallback. Nothing else on the image provides that service. So Pictures, Downloads and the Ristretto strip show generic icons, and she sees that every time she opens a photo folder. The fix works as proposed: tumbler's desktop-thumbnailer plugin loads *.thumbnailer files, so the evince, librsvg and ffmpegthumbnailer thumbnailers all work. Adding tumbler is 3 packages, and tumbler with ffmpegthumbnailer is 5 packages, both about 1.3 MB. Do not use tumbler-plugins-extra (it pulls in WebKit).

Not a defect. The finding itself says leave dropped. libreoffice-gtk3 only Recommends it, and it would be useless alone, because the image lacks the audio sinks and the demuxers and decoders (gstreamer1.0-plugins-good, -pulseaudio or -pipewire, -libav). Only embedded media in Writer or Calc documents is affected, which is rare.

Not a defect. GNOME Software is the only GTK4 program, and only the rare video screenshot on an app page would be empty. The finding itself says leave dropped, and the decoders it would need are not installed either.

No user-visible effect. mpv's shipped /etc/mpv/mpv.conf sets hwdec=vaapi, and without a VA driver mpv falls back silently to software decoding. The finding's own test shows this, and the compositor has no dmabuf path anyway.
No effect. mpv's config uses vaapi only, so nothing on the image uses VDPAU.
No effect. mpv has no way for her to enter a web URL on this image. The archive's yt-dlp is also stale and would pull in 10 packages.
Negligible. It matters only for AACS-encrypted commercial Blu-rays, which needs an optical drive and a user-supplied KEYDB.cfg. Unencrypted discs, ISO files and BDMV folders play without it.

Confirmed docs-only. dpkg -c shows just changelog.Debian.gz and copyright. The PipeWire configs come from pipewire-bin (/usr/share/pipewire/pipewire.conf and client.conf), which I verified with dpkg -S.

Not worth acting on. USB webcams use PipeWire's V4L2 plugin, which is installed. MIPI/IPU6 cameras also need out-of-tree drivers, and the hardware stream already reports "camera won't work yet" for that class. The WirePlumber warning is harmless.
No effect. libpocketsphinx3 is present only because libavfilter9 (from mpv) depends on it, and only ffmpeg's asr filter uses the model. The 36 MB model is not worth shipping.

findings.what_breaks: Plugging in a USB printer that is not IPP-over-USB creates no print queue. That covers every printer the image says it handles through printer-driver-hpcups and printer-driver-gutenprint, meaning older HP, Epson and Canon models. The package ships the udev rule 70-printers.rules, the configure-printer@.service unit and udev-configure-printer/udev-add-printer, which auto-create the queue with the right PPD. Nothing else in the image does this, so the Print dialog lists no printer until she opens Printers and adds it by hand.
findings.how_she_notices: She plugs in the printer she has owned for 15 years, presses Print from Letters or the browser, and the printer is not in the list. The driver packages are installed but never used until she finds the 'Printers' tile and works through Add.
findings.evidence: .deb contents: lib/udev/rules.d/70-printers.rules (fires on ID_USB_INTERFACES '*:0701??:*' except 070104, with SYSTEMD_WANTS=configure-printer@usb-BUS-DEV.service), lib/systemd/system/configure-printer@.service (ExecStart=/lib/udev/udev-configure-printer add), lib/udev/udev-add-printer (python: cupshelpers matches the device ID to a PPD, then c.addPrinter and activateNewPrinter). The rule deliberately skips 7/1/4 because that is ipp-usb's case. Not present in the closure install (no 70-printers.rules). All its Depends are already in the image (python3-cups, python3-cupshelpers, python3-dbus, libusb-1.0-0, libcups2t64, libudev1). No AurOS code creates queues: grep of src, rootfs and build at origin/main finds no lpadmin or lpinfo calls. tools/hardenboottest.sh:238-250 adds its test queue by hand with `lpadmin -m everywhere`. hw/lib/hwcompat.c:352-360 reports 'works' ('printer-model-driver: CUPS has a driver for this model (HP hpcups or Gutenprint) in the image') for USB printers, but that verdict is only true after a manual add. docs/handoff/streams/S1.md:49 says 'A real USB printer is unproven'. The manual path exists: forge:742 renames system-config-printer to 'Printers', and the cups-pk-helper polkit grants are in place.
findings.fix: Add system-config-printer-udev to packages_hardware in profiles/desktop.profile next to system-config-printer. Add an imagetest assert for /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/70-printers.rules, or the /lib/udev/ equivalent, plus a mutant. If she should never have to touch Printers, consider a tiny AurOS oneshot that runs `lpadmin -m everywhere` for printers found by ippfind. It opens no listener, unlike cups-browsed.

findings.what_breaks: udisks' Drive.Eject method works by running the external command `eject <device>`. With no eject binary the job fails, gvfs passes the error up, and Thunar shows a 'Failed to eject' dialog. gvfs has already unmounted the volume by then, so no data is at risk, but the error appears on a routine action. It hits drives where Thunar takes the eject path and not the safely-remove (power-off) path: SD cards in a reader or the built-in slot, CD/DVD drives, and any USB stick not on udisks' short 'thumb drive' list that reports removable=1.
findings.how_she_notices: She presses the eject arrow beside her camera's SD card, a DVD or a USB stick. The disk icon disappears, then an error box says it could not be ejected, and she is left unsure whether it is safe to pull.
findings.evidence: udisks2 2.10.1 src/udiskslinuxdrive.c:1105-1118 handle_eject spawns "eject %s" and returns 'Error ejecting %s: %s' on failure. The string 'eject %s' is in /usr/libexec/udisks2/udisksd in the installed closure, and /usr/bin/eject is absent there. gvfs monitor/udisks2/gvfsudisks2drive.c:215 sets can_eject from udisks 'ejectable' (sysfs removable=1). Lines 243-278 allow can_stop (power-off, no eject binary) only when !is_media_removable && !coldplug. eject_cb returns the error to the caller. Thunar thunar-device.c:818-848 tries g_drive_stop first, else g_drive_eject_with_operation. udisks drive_media_mapping (udiskslinuxdrive.c:363+) makes ID_DRIVE_THUMB drives non-removable, but 80-udisks2.rules:101-105 sets ID_DRIVE_THUMB only for Kingston DataTraveler, SanDisk Cruzer, HP v125w, Patriot and JetFlash/Transcend. ID_DRIVE_FLASH_SD and ID_CDROM* are force_removable, so they use eject. build/forge ~2144-2150 deliberately grants org.freedesktop.udisks2.eject-media and power-off-drive ('Thunar's safely remove'), so this path is intended to work. eject is not in the manifest, and it is only a udisks2 Recommends.
findings.fix: Add eject to packages_files in profiles/desktop.profile (udisks2 line). It Depends only on libc6 and libmount1. Add an imagetest assert for /usr/bin/eject.

findings.what_breaks: An iPhone or iPad plugged in by cable never appears in Files. gvfs-backends hard-depends on libimobiledevice6, libusbmuxd6 and libplist, so the client half of the afc backend is installed and has nothing to talk to. The daemon that multiplexes the phone's USB connection is only in usbmuxd.
findings.how_she_notices: She plugs in her iPhone to get photos off it, as WP-25 expected ('Phone photos import'), and nothing shows up in Files. The phone itself does ask 'Trust this computer?', but only once usbmuxd is running.
findings.evidence: gvfs 1.54.4 monitor/afc/afcvolumemonitor.c:103 calls idevice_event_subscribe(). That goes through libimobiledevice to libusbmuxd, which connects to the usbmuxd socket (/var/run/usbmuxd) and never sees a device when the daemon is absent. The usbmuxd .deb ships /usr/sbin/usbmuxd, usbmuxd.service and 39-usbmuxd.rules, which matches PRODUCT 5ac/12[9a]x/* and 5ac/8600/*, sets SYSTEMD_WANTS=usbmuxd.service and runs as user usbmux. In the closure install /usr/sbin/usbmuxd and 39-usbmuxd.rules do not exist. Only libusbmuxd6 and libimobiledevice6 are in the manifest. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md:189 (WP-25) lists 'usbmuxd, libimobiledevice-utils'. It never landed, and grep of build, profiles and rootfs for usbmuxd finds nothing. The profile comment motivating heif-gdk-pixbuf ('a photo from an iPhone') shows iPhone photos are expected. No AurOS-side import path exists (grep of src for afc, mtp, DCIM and usbmux finds nothing).
findings.fix: Add usbmuxd to packages_files in profiles/desktop.profile. libimobiledevice-utils is not needed: the gvfs afc backend does its own pairing. Add an imagetest assert for /usr/sbin/usbmuxd and 39-usbmuxd.rules.

Thunar has no built-in thumbnailer: it only asks the org.xfce.Tumbler D-Bus service. This overlaps the graphics/icons area; I include it because phone and camera photo folders are the place she notices it first.

The tumbler .deb ships tumblerd, the org.xfce.Tumbler.* dbus service files, and plugins for pixbuf, jpeg, poppler (PDF), font, desktop and gst. Not in the manifest. docs/PLAN-END-TO-END.md:189 (WP-25) lists tumbler and ffmpegthumbnailer as to-add, and they never landed.
findings.fix: Add tumbler (not tumbler-plugins-extra) to packages_files in profiles/desktop.profile. Do NOT add tumbler-plugins-extra: apt simulation shows it drags libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0 and libjavascriptcoregtk (+139 MB installed). The base tumbler already covers images and PDFs. ffmpegthumbnailer (0.28 MB) gives video thumbnails, if wanted. Add an imagetest assert for tumblerd.

findings.what_breaks: The udev rules 55-dm.rules, 60-persistent-storage-dm.rules and 95-dm-notify.rules ship only in dmsetup. libdevmapper (used by libcryptsetup, hence by udisks2/libblockdev unlock of an encrypted USB stick) waits on a udev cookie that only 95-dm-notify.rules completes. This is derived from source and not run, because it needs a privileged host with device-mapper. The wait is a semop loop with no timeout, so unlocking a LUKS stick would block forever. The S4 disk-lock switch-on also installs only cryptsetup-bin, which would hit the same wait in lockctl.
findings.how_she_notices: Today: a LUKS-encrypted USB stick (say one a relative encrypted) gets a passphrase prompt and then spins forever, even though the image's polkit rule grants encrypted-unlock for this. After S4 is switched on, the lockctl and cryptsetup calls on the live system would hang.
findings.evidence: lvm2 2.03.16 libdm/libdm-common.c:2729-2780 _udev_wait does `while (semop(semid, &sb, 1) < 0) { if (errno==EINTR) goto repeat_wait; ...}` with no timeout. It is used whenever dm_udev_get_sync_support() is true (udev running, per _check_udev_is_running at 2320). cryptsetup 2.7.0 lib/libdevmapper.c:1292-1363 and 1383-1407 call dm_task_set_cookie then _dm_udev_wait for every activate and remove. The dmsetup .deb is the only file provider of 95-dm-notify.rules (`RUN+="/sbin/dmsetup udevcomplete $env{DM_COOKIE}"`) and 55-dm.rules. apt-cache: libdevmapper1.02.1 only Recommends dmsetup, libcryptsetup12 and cryptsetup-bin don't depend on it, and only the 'cryptsetup' package does. ENV{ID_MTP_DEVICE}="1"`. findings.what_breaks: Already tracked as docs/security/FINDINGS.md SEC-065 (Low) and still not in the profile: Intel thermal daemon absent, so dusty 2013-era Intel laptops rely on the kernel's own throttling and can reach the critical trip and power off abruptly. Intel only; it exits on other CPUs.
findings.how_she_notices: An old Intel laptop under load, with a clogged fan, shuts off suddenly with no warning.
findings.evidence: SEC-065 text: '`thermald` not installed (dropped as a Recommends)... Add `thermald` to `packages_hardware`'. grep of profiles, build and rootfs for thermald finds nothing. The thermald .deb ships /usr/sbin/thermald, thermald.service and a dbus policy, and Depends additionally on libdbus-glib-1-2 and libupower-glib3 (the library only, not the upower daemon). aurshell reads the battery from /sys/class/power_supply directly (src/aurshell/power.c:24) and does its own critical-battery sleep (watch.c:50-60), so upower itself is not needed.
findings.fix: Add thermald to packages_hardware per SEC-065, and verify `systemctl is-active thermald` on Intel and a clean exit on AMD.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. It is absent from the shipped manifest (fc52718 PACKAGES.txt; the profile diff since then is only librsvg2-common). Neither wireplumber nor pipewire-pulse depends on it, and nothing else in the image offers Bluetooth audio (no bluealsa, no pulseaudio). The libspa-0.2-modules .deb has no bluez5 directory, while the libspa-0.2-bluetooth .deb is the only provider of spa-0.2/bluez5/libspa-bluez5.so and the codec plugins. wireplumber's bluez.lua:393-397 logs "PipeWire's BlueZ SPA missing or broken. Bluetooth not supported." when it is missing. The aurshell bt.h header advertises the "Headphones and mice" panel, and WP-25 planned this package but it never landed. Real gap, and cheap to fix (about 1.4 MB, dependencies are small libs).

Confirmed. It is absent from the manifest and is only a Recommends of system-config-printer and system-config-printer-common. Its .deb is the only source of 70-printers.rules, configure-printer@.service and udev-add-printer, which call addPrinter with a matched PPD. The rule fires for USB printer-class devices and skips 7/1/4 (ipp-usb's case), so an older non-IPP-USB printer gets no queue without it. printer-driver-hpcups and gutenprint are installed but never used until she adds the printer by hand. python3-cups, python3-cupshelpers and python3-dbus are already in the image. No AurOS code runs lpadmin. Real gap, tiny cost (about 20 KB).

Confirmed from source. udisks2 2.10.1 handle_eject (udiskslinuxdrive.c:1105-1118) spawns "eject <dev>" and returns "Error ejecting" if that fails. The eject binary is absent from the manifest (it is only a udisks2 Recommends). gvfs gvfsudisks2drive.c uses can_stop (power-off) only for non-removable media, so SD cards (mmcblk is forced ejectable), optical drives and removable-flag USB sticks go through g_drive_eject. Thunar tries stop first, then eject, and shows a "Failed to eject" dialog on error (thunar-action-manager.c:3069). forge grants eject-media on purpose, so this path is meant to work. Data is safe because gvfs unmounts first, but a CD tray will not open and a routine action shows an error. Real gap, trivial cost (about 25 KB).

The claim that an iPhone never appears in Files does not hold. usbmuxd is only needed for the AFC backend. The image ships gvfs-backends with gvfs-gphoto2-volume-monitor and libgphoto2-6t64. The libgphoto2 hwdb marks Apple 05ac:12a8 (iPhone 5 and later) and 12ab (iPad Air) as ID_GPHOTO2=1 in PTP mode. The libgphoto2 rules also tag any 6/1/1 interface as ID_GPHOTO2, and systemd's 70-uaccess.rules gives the seat user access. gvfs's gphoto2 monitor has no Apple or AFC exclusion, and libgphoto2 ptp2 has iOS-specific handling (library.c:10119). So the phone shows up as a camera with its photos, which is the stated need (phone photos import, with HEIC handled by heif-gdk-pixbuf). I could not test with a real phone, so the claim stays unproven. AFC would only add full-file access, which she does not need.

Confirmed. It is absent from the manifest and is a Recommends of thunar and ristretto. Thunar 4.18.8 has no thumbnailer of its own. It only requests thumbnails over D-Bus from org.freedesktop.thumbnails.Thumbnailer1 (thunar-thumbnailer.c:806-817), which tumbler provides, and icon-factory only loads thumbnail files that already exist. Without it every photo or PDF is a generic icon in Files. The plain tumbler package (not -plugins-extra) covers pixbuf, jpeg, poppler, font and gst, and its dependencies (poppler-glib, gstreamer, cairo, pixbuf) are already installed. WP-25 planned it and it never landed. Real UX gap, about 1 MB.

Confirmed by source, not by a run. A run needs a privileged host with a live udev, which I did not set up. libdm's _udev_wait (libdm-common.c:2729-2780) loops on semop with no timeout, and it is active whenever udev is running. cryptsetup 2.7.0 (lib/libdevmapper.c:1330-1363, 1400-1407) waits on a cookie for every activate and remove. The only provider of 95-dm-notify.rules (udevcomplete) and 55-dm.rules is the dmsetup .deb. The udev .deb has no dm rules, and dmsetup is absent from the manifest (libdevmapper1.02.1 only Recommends it). So unlocking a LUKS or BitLocker stick through udisks would block forever. forge grants encrypted-unlock on purpose. The frequency is low, since only an encrypted stick triggers it, but the cost is about 80 KB and the failure is a hang. Keep it, rated medium to low.

Confirmed but low. 69-libmtp.rules falls back to /usr/lib/udev/mtp-probe for devices missing from the hwdb, and that binary ships only in libmtp-runtime (absent from the manifest). gvfs-mtp gates on ID_MTP_DEVICE (gmtpvolume.c:105, gmtpvolumemonitor.c:241), so unlisted phones are ignored. The 1412-entry hwdb covers the main vendors (Google, Samsung, Xiaomi, Huawei, Motorola, HTC, OnePlus, Oppo and others), so she will rarely hit it. I keep it because WP-25 planned this package, PARITY.md claims libmtp landed, and the fix is 6 KB with no new dependencies.

The finding's own fix is to keep cups-browsed out, so there is no package to add. The purge in build/harden is deliberate (CVE-2024-47176), and the profile comment says printing works without it. Nothing in the image regressed. GTK print dialogs browse DNS-SD printers themselves. The remaining gap is that LibreOffice lists only configured queues. That is a design and UX question (queue creation via the Printers tile), not a dropped-Recommends bug. I did not verify the LibreOffice behavior.

The finding itself says to leave it out, so it is not a fix. Adding it without PAM auto-unlock would raise a create-keyring password prompt, which is worse for her. gvfs only tries to store a password when she picks Remember in the prompt, and the default is forget. The dependency check shows it is only a Recommends of gvfs-backends and software-properties-gtk. No action.

Unproven benefit. This is not a regression or a broken feature, and docs/security/FINDINGS.md already tracks it as SEC-065 (Low). thermald does not prevent the kernel's critical-trip shutdown. Old 2013 ACPI laptops are throttled by the kernel's passive trips and by hardware thermal control. thermald matters mostly for newer DPTF-style platforms, and it is known to over-throttle some older CPUs, which would hurt the slow machines AurOS targets. It is only a Recommends of linux-image-generic. A design call, not a defect.

CONFIRMED from source. udisks2 2.10.1 (udiskslinuxdrive.c) runs the external command 'eject <dev>' for Drive.Eject and returns 'Error ejecting <dev>' when it fails. Ejectable is just the sysfs 'removable' flag. The only sticks that skip it are those udisks marks ID_DRIVE_THUMB (named Kingston DataTraveler, SanDisk Cruzer, a few others), because they are then non-removable and get power-off. Other sticks, SD cards in readers and CD/DVD report removable=1. For them gvfs sets can_eject, and can_stop is false because media is removable. Thunar 4.18 therefore calls g_drive_eject_with_operation, which becomes Drive.Eject and the 'eject' spawn. The simulated closure and the real forge log both lack eject (udisks2 only Recommends it). build/forge grants udisks2.eject-media polkit specifically for this flow. She gets an error dialog after the volume is already unmounted. Not run on real hardware.

findings.what_breaks: PipeWire, WirePlumber and pipewire-pulse cannot get realtime or raised priority, so the audio thread stays an ordinary time-shared thread. The rlimit route is also closed, so nothing else gives them priority either.
findings.how_she_notices: Music or a video call crackles or drops out when anything else is using the CPU (LibreOffice opening, a heavy web page, Zoom's video) on a dual-core 2013 laptop. Not measured on real hardware, so this is plausible rather than proven.
findings.evidence: Test: noble container with the desktop.profile + store + flatpak package set (882 packages, no Recommends), pipewire 1.0.5 run as a non-root user without rtkit. The log says: 'failed to set realtime policy: Operation not permitted', 'Priority max (0) must be at least 11', then 'Realtime scheduling disabled: unsufficient realtime privileges, Portal not found on session bus, and no system bus for RTKit'. WirePlumber and pipewire-pulse log the same line. ps shows pw-data-loop as class TS (normal), nice 0. The container had no system bus; on AurOS there is one but no org.freedesktop.RealtimeKit1 service, so the outcome is the same. The only other route is pipewire's /etc/security/limits.d/25-pw-rlimits.conf, which applies only to group @pipewire. build/forge AUROS_GROUPS_WANT is 'audio video input netdev bluetooth lpadmin' (~line 1753), so no pipewire group. docs/handoff/streams/F.md already lists 'RealtimeKit missing' as noise in a booted AurOS journal (run 40016668568). rtkit would be allowed: its polkit actions acquire-real-time and acquire-high-priority are allow_active=yes. aurshell.service has PAMName=, so the session is a logind session, and rootfs 49-auros.rules only returns YES for listed actions and leaves the rest to the defaults. NOT tested: whether the realtime grant succeeds, because the container lacks CAP_SYS_RESOURCE.
findings.fix: Add rtkit to packages_desktop next to pipewire (it is D-Bus activated, so no boot cost until pipewire asks). All its dependencies are already in the image: dbus, polkitd, libcap2, adduser. Zero-package alternative: add the 'pipewire' group to AUROS_GROUPS_WANT. The group is created by pipewire's postinst, and rootfs/etc/pam.d/systemd-user already has pam_limits.so. To check on a booted image: journalctl --user -u pipewire shows no 'Realtime scheduling disabled', and chrt -p $(pgrep -x pipewire) is not SCHED_OTHER.

LibreOffice itself depends on no dictionary, so dropping or swapping Mousepad would silently remove Writer's spell check. (b) LibreOffice finds only en-US. For any other language (en-GB, en-AU, en-CA, es, fr, de ...) there is no dictionary, so no spell check at all. The installer hands the Windows language to the image without asking (src/aurbridge/wizard.c detect_defaults, rootfs/usr/lib/auros/choices.sh sets LANG). LibreOffice's default document language follows LANG, which I expect but did not test. (c) Hyphenation and thesaurus do not exist in any language. hyphen-en-us and mythes-en-us are Recommended only by the task-* desktop metapackages, so they were never on the dropped list.
findings.how_she_notices: For a British, Australian, Canadian, Spanish or French Windows user, Writer never underlines a misspelling, and she believes her letter is fine. Thesaurus and hyphenation menu entries do nothing. A US-English user notices nothing today.
findings.evidence: LibreOffice 24.2.7 on the full package set, queried over UNO. Spell locales: [en-US] only; hyphenator locales: []; thesaurus locales: []. hasLocale(en-GB), (fr-FR) and (es-ES) are all False. libmergedlo.so contains the paths '/usr/share/hunspell' and DICPATH, so en_US.dic/.aff in /usr/share/hunspell is what it loads. apt-cache depends libenchant-2-2 shows '|Depends: hunspell-en-us'. hunspell-en-us is also in the 'additional packages' list of the real office-profile build log (release profiles-40042856709, office-build.log.gz), next to libenchant-2-2 and libgspell-1-2. findings.fix: Name hunspell-en-us in packages_files so it is manually installed and survives Mousepad changes (0.9 MB). If the product ships outside the US, add hunspell-en-gb (2.6 MB), hunspell-en-au and hunspell-en-ca (0.9 MB each). For other languages, have choices.sh or the multilingual profile add hunspell-<lang> for the chosen LANG: hunspell-es 2.0 MB, hunspell-de-de 1.9 MB, hunspell-fr-classical 2.9 MB. Optionally add hyphen-en-us (0.14 MB). Skip mythes-en-us (21.5 MB).

findings.pkg: ibus-gtk3, ibus-gtk4, im-config (Recommends of ibus) and language-pack-gnome-<lang> (multilingual profile only)
findings.recommended_by: ibus (the three input-method pieces); language-pack-gnome-<lang> is not a Recommends of language-pack-<lang>
findings.what_breaks: Applies only to profiles/multilingual.profile (the desktop profile ships no IME by design). Its packages_extra installs ibus, ibus-pinyin, ibus-m17n and language-pack-fr/-zh-hans/-es/-ar under --no-install-recommends. (1) ibus installs without its GTK input-method modules (im-ibus.so is in ibus-gtk3, libim-ibus.so in ibus-gtk4) and without im-config, which sets the environment. (2) Nothing starts ibus-daemon. I found no XDG-autostart or Xsession handling in src/aurshell, build/ or rootfs/, and im-config only works through /etc/X11/Xsession.d and /etc/xdg/autostart. aurwl compiles in text-input-v3 only when wishes=on, and never input-method. So Pinyin cannot be typed even with the Recommends added back; the session also has to start ibus-daemon and set GTK_IM_MODULE. (3) language-pack-fr Depends only on language-pack-fr-base. The GTK/GNOME strings (gtk30.mo, gtk40.mo, gnome-software.mo, evince.mo, system-config-printer.mo) are in language-pack-gnome-fr-base, which nothing pulls in.
findings.how_she_notices: A Chinese user of the multilingual build cannot type Chinese in any program. French, Spanish and Arabic users get an English file chooser, store, PDF viewer, printer dialog, LibreOffice and Firefox, although the profile says 'ready to go'.
findings.evidence: apt-cache depends ibus gives Recommends ibus-gtk, ibus-gtk3, ibus-gtk4, im-config. dpkg -c on ibus-gtk3 and ibus-gtk4 shows the immodules above; im-config ships Xsession.d/70im-config_launch plus xdg/autostart/im-launch.desktop. The desktop image's /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gtk-3.0/3.0.0/immodules lists im-am-et ... im-xim and no im-ibus. dpkg -c language-pack-fr-base contains only core strings (NetworkManager.mo, cups.mo, polkit-1.mo), while language-pack-gnome-fr-base holds the GTK ones. After installing all 882 packages, /usr/share/locale/fr/LC_MESSAGES is empty, because Ubuntu strips .mo files out of the packages. aurwl: build/forge ~1110 and 1183 compile text-input only if wishes_on.
findings.fix: packages_extra += ibus-gtk3 ibus-gtk4 plus language-pack-gnome-{fr,zh-hans,es,ar} and libreoffice-l10n-{fr,zh-cn,es,ar}, plus the dictionaries from the previous finding. Add a session step (aurshell or a systemd --user unit) that starts 'ibus-daemon -drx' and sets GTK_IM_MODULE=ibus and XMODIFIERS when ibus is present; without it the packages do nothing. Check on a booted multilingual image that typing Pinyin works in Mousepad and in Firefox.
findings.cost_mb: ibus-gtk3 0.07 + ibus-gtk4 0.08 + im-config 0.34; each gnome language pack 8-12 installed (2.5 download); libreoffice-l10n ~4.5 per language

findings.pkg: language-pack-<lang>-base, language-pack-gnome-<lang>-base, libreoffice-l10n-<lang> (never Recommended by anything installed, so not on the dropped list); the dropped *-l10n packages are harmless
findings.recommended_by: none (the dropped debconf-i18n, e2fsprogs-l10n, gnupg-l10n, krb5-locales, libgpg-error-l10n, libgphoto2-l10n and ubuntu-pro-client-l10n only translate command-line and back-end messages)
findings.what_breaks: On the desktop profile, when the installer carries over a non-English Windows language, LANG becomes e.g. fr_FR.UTF-8 (locales is installed and locale-gen works), but no translated strings are installed. Ubuntu moves every .mo out of its packages into the language packs, so GTK apps, GNOME Software, LibreOffice and Firefox all stay English. aurshell is English-only today, so the result is an all-English desktop with a foreign date and number format. This is a product decision rather than a regression.
findings.how_she_notices: A French or Spanish speaker finds every menu in English. The seven dropped l10n packages (about 1.6 MB together) change nothing she can see.
findings.evidence: With all 882 packages installed, /usr/share/locale/fr/LC_MESSAGES is empty. The French strings live only in language-pack-fr-base (13.9 MB installed) and language-pack-gnome-fr-base (12.0 MB installed). src/aurbridge/wizard.c:1733 maps the Windows locale name to a glibc name. build/forge ~222 says the language chosen in the installer 'had nothing to be generated with' before locales was added, and only locale-gen was fixed. The forge comment for the renamed apps already says names stay English until AurOS carries its own translations.
findings.fix: Decide whether non-English is supported in v0.1. If not, say so in the product copy and leave the l10n packages dropped. If yes, have first boot (choices.sh) install language-pack-<lang>, language-pack-gnome-<lang>, libreoffice-l10n-<lang> and hunspell-<lang> for the chosen LANG when online, or ship the top few languages in the image.
findings.cost_mb: per language ~25-30 installed (~6 MB download) plus libreoffice-l10n ~4.5

Rootless Xwayland (aurwl xwm.inc: -rootless -wm) draws no frames, and aurwl offers xdg-decoration server-side to every toplevel (aurwl.c:3039-3100), so a plugin could only add a second title bar. xauth (0.07 MB): aurwl starts Xwayland with no -auth; xauth is a CLI for cookie files; the repo's own wltest-apps image (VLC, Zoom and Discord drawn through aurwl's Xwayland) installs xwayland with --no-install-recommends and no xauth. xfonts-base (7.2 MB): Xwayland carries the 'built-ins' font path (fixed and cursor); only legacy core-font clients (xlsfonts, old Tk/Motif/Java) would fail, and the same harness runs xterm/x11-apps without it. x11-utils and x11-xserver-utils (0.65 and 0.56 MB): no code in src/, build/ or rootfs/ calls xrandr, xset, xprop, xrdb or xmodmap. Only xdg-screensaver's generic X path uses xset, and it needs DISPLAY. libfile-mimeinfo-perl, libnet-dbus-perl and libx11-protocol-perl (0.1 to 0.6 MB): only xdg-open's generic fallback (mimeopen) and xdg-screensaver's gnome-screensaver branch use them; AurOS diverts xdg-open to a gio-open wrapper (build/forge stage_xdg_open, rootfs/usr/bin/xdg-open). systemd-hwe-hwdb (16 KB): the noble-updates version holds only two mic-mute key rules (Dell Pro Rugged, HP EliteBoard); 60-keyboard.hwdb is in udev. groff-base (3.7 MB): no man pages or terminal. libgtk-3-bin, libgtk-4-bin (0.3 and 12 MB) and libgdk-pixbuf2.0-bin: only CLI helpers. gtk-update-icon-cache is its own installed package, and the GTK3 immodules.cache exists. verdicts.reason: Facts hold, severity is overstated (medium -> low). CONFIRMED: apt-cache shows pipewire-bin Recommends rtkit. The real office and multilingual build logs (release profiles-40042856709) list rtkit under 'Recommended packages' and not installed, and no profile or forge line names it. I reproduced pipewire 1.0.5 as a non-root user without rtkit: 'Realtime scheduling disabled', and pw-data-loop runs as TS, nice 0. Nothing else provides it. The rlimit file 25-pw-rlimits.conf applies only to @pipewire, and AUROS_GROUPS_WANT has no pipewire group. xdg-desktop-portal's Realtime portal is only an RTKit client (its binary references org.freedesktop.RealtimeKit1). The fix should work: the rtkit policy has allow_inactive=yes and allow_active=yes. Polkit 124's session monitor falls back to sd_uid_get_display() for processes in user@.service, so pipewire resolves to aurshell's PAM session. rtkit's deps are already present and it is 34 KB. NOT CONFIRMED: music crackling. I pinned non-RT pipewire and a playing stream to 2 cores with 5 CPU hogs (2.5x oversubscribed), 20 s each. At the default 1024/48000 and at 512 there were no extra xruns (1 per run, the same as the unloaded baseline). At 256/48000 (5 ms) there were 10-16 xruns against 1 unloaded. So only low-latency clients such as calls, under heavy load, would glitch. Not tested: the actual grant on a booted AurOS.

verdicts.pkg: hunspell-en-us (kept only by accident) and hunspell-<lang>, hyphen-en-us, mythes-en-us
verdicts.reason: Only the en-GB/en-AU/en-CA/other-language dictionary gap survives; the rest is refuted. REFUTED: hunspell-en-us is not absent. It is in the NEW-packages list of the real office and multilingual build logs (via mousepad -> libgspell -> libenchant-2-2), and libhunspell-1.7-0's Recommends is satisfied. 'Kept by accident' is fragility, not a break today. hyphen-en-us and mythes-en-us are recommended by nothing installed (only task-* metas; the libreoffice metapackage merely Suggests them). Hyphenation is off by default and no thesaurus is expected. CONFIRMED (I ran headless LibreOffice 24.2 over UNO in noble): with libreoffice-writer alone, no dictionary exists. With hunspell-en-us added, hasLocale is True only for en-US and False for en-GB, en-AU, en-CA, fr, es and de. A new Writer document's CharLocale follows LANG: LANG=en_GB.UTF-8 gives en-GB. The chain is real. wizard.c detect_defaults turns Windows 'en-GB' into en_GB.UTF-8, the wizard lists 'English (United Kingdom)', and choices.sh generates the locale and writes /etc/default/locale. So a UK, AU or CA user gets a document language with no dictionary and Writer underlines nothing. Fix: hunspell-en-gb 2.6 MB, hunspell-en-au and hunspell-en-ca 0.9 MB each. Naming hunspell-en-us in packages_files (0.9 MB) is a cheap extra. Strictly this is locale coverage, not a dropped Recommends.

Nothing in src, build, rootfs or tools mentions ibus beyond the profile line, so nothing starts ibus-daemon. REFUTED AS A SHIPPED-IMAGE DEFECT: (1) multilingual is not what she gets. The wizard always writes 'desktop' (docs/issues/v3/05-installer-wizard.md 5.4), and the release assets contain only the desktop image. The multilingual build is a CI recipe whose log says update_channel=off. The desktop profile has no IME by design. (2) Adding the Recommends would not make Pinyin work. It needs a new session feature (start ibus-daemon, set GTK_IM_MODULE and XMODIFIERS), so this is a feature gap in an edition, not a missed dependency. (3) The English-only GTK strings are an already documented known issue (5.6: apps whose translations are in Ubuntu language packs stay English). Track it as multilingual-edition work, not as a dropped-Recommends fix.

Verified myself: libpipewire-0.3-common holds only changelog and copyright. pipewire, pipewire-pulse and wireplumber ran without it and 'pactl info' answered. The dropped xdg-utils Recommends (libfile-mimeinfo-perl, libnet-dbus-perl, libx11-protocol-perl, x11-utils, x11-xserver-utils) are used only by xdg-utils' generic fallbacks. xdg-open is diverted to gio (build/forge stage_xdg_open). Neither is installed, which is the exit-4 failure the repo already found and sidestepped for xdg-open only. No shipped program was found calling it. Second, outside this list, tumbler (a Thunar Recommends) appears unrecommended-and-absent in the real build log, so Thunar probably shows no image thumbnails.
